rationale: This is the archive's Counterparty_Versus_Market_Funding_Mix with `dltis` deleted from a two-term issuance aggregate — a component-level rescaling of the arms-length leg dressed up as an information-hierarchy claim, and the promised Sharpe gain is a portfolio-efficiency conjecture rather than a new mechanism.

xrd/(xrd+|gross profit|) is a monotone transform of R&D-to-gross-profit and therefore a highly correlated substitute for the MA(xrd/sale) conditioner already paired with this exact counterparty-change leg (Counterparty_Funded_Innovation), so the proposal is largely an intersection of two archive signals with a different intensity denominator rather than a new state variable.

Replacing LAG(DELTA(xrd/sale)) with LAG(TREND(xrd/sale,3)) in Counterparties_Follow_The_Research_Ramp is a smoothing/window knob, not a distinct economic claim, and it additionally pushes the conditioning window back to t-4..t-2 while cutting history-dependent coverage for no clearly identified new mechanism.

Direct rediscovery of Delayed_Market_Funding_After_Withdrawal with the issuance term narrowed from sstk+dltis to sstk — a one-term deletion aimed at nudging a t-stat of −1.79 over the line, which is exactly the cosmetic variant the objective warns against.

Genuinely inverts the sequencing logic — conditioning on lagged counterparty support and sorting on the firm's subsequent research response — so both tails are ecosystem-validated firms separated by reinvestment behaviour, an economically distinct claim from the archive's investment-then-funding tests, with the interaction's sign direction correctly matching the stated hypothesis.

This is the arithmetic union of Counterparty_Support_Despite_Revenue_Decline (conditioner unchanged) and the already-flagged equity-only tweak of the funding leg, so it adds no mechanism beyond the two archive components it stacks and risks compounding their coverage and composition instability.
